source_title: Landstar Investigation Notice: SueWallSt Notifies Investors of Pending Investigation Into Landstar (LSTR)
source_excerpt:
Previews positioned Landstar as an earnings-beat candidate heading into its October 27 report. Instead, the quarter fell short of analyst expectations on earnings and LSTR shares dropped. SueWallSt notifies investors of a pending investigation into potential securities law violations on behalf of affected investors.
NEW YORK , Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Wall Street was looking for a beat when Landstar System, Inc. (NASDAQ: LSTR ) reported third-quarter results after the close on October 27, 2026. Instead, earnings came in below analyst expectations and shares fell more than 15%. If you bought LSTR heading into that report and are now holding a loss, you may have legal rights. Shareholders who lost money on Landstar are encouraged to submit your loss details for a free case review today. You may also contact Joseph E. Levi, Esq. via email at [email protected] or by telephone at (888) SueWallSt.
Headed into the print, analysts reportedly were expecting earnings per share of approximately $1.62 to $1.67. Landstar reported EPS of just $1.42. In its release, Landstar noted it was "negatively impacted by highly elevated insurance and claim costs." Elaborating during the earnings call, CEO Frank Lonegro noted they had "approximately $22 million of net unfavorable adjustments to prior year claim estimates," comprised of $13 million in unfavorable adjustments and reserves and $8 million from the settlement of two claims. Reportedly, insurance and claim expenses rose to $55.3 million from $33.0 million in the prior-year period, hurting bottom-line performance despite top-line growth.
If the post-earnings decline cost you money on LSTR, request a confidential evaluation of your losses or call Joseph E. Levi, Esq. at (888) SueWallSt.

Frequently Asked Questions About the LSTR Investigation
Q: How much did LSTR stock drop? A: Shares opened down approximately $25.65, or about 15% on October 28, 2026, following investor reaction to Landstar System, Inc.'s (NASDAQ: LSTR ) reported third-quarter results. Investors who purchased shares at allegedly inflated prices and suffered losses may be eligible to seek compensation.
Q: Which statements are being investigated as potentially misleading? A: The investigation concerns whether Landstar may have made misleading statements or may not have adequately disclosed information regarding its third-quarter profitability. After the Company reported earnings below analyst expectations on October 27, 2026, the stock price declined 15% by the time the market opened the following morning.
Q: What do LSTR investors need to do right now? A: Investors may gather brokerage records showing purchase dates, share quantities, and prices paid. Submit your information for a no-cost, no-obligation evaluation of your potential recovery . No immediate action is required to remain eligible to participate in the investigation.
Q: What documents do I need to participate? A: Brokerage statements or trade confirmations showing purchase dates, share quantities, prices paid, and any subsequent sale dates and prices.
Q: What if I already sold my LSTR shares -- can I still recover losses? A: Yes. Eligibility is based on when you purchased, not whether you still hold the shares. Investors who bought LSTR and sold at a loss may still participate in the investigation.
Q: What if my LSTR losses are small -- is it still worth contacting a lawyer? A: Yes. There is no minimum loss amount required to participate in the investigation.
Q: Do I need to go to court or give testimony? A: No. Participating in the investigation does not require court appearances or depositions. If legal action is later pursued, the overwhelming majority of affected investors never appear in court either.
Q: What does it cost me to participate? A: There is no upfront cost to submit your information and review whether you may be eligible to recover. Should you choose to participate in any resulting action, these matters are generally handled on a contingency basis, with any attorneys' fees and expenses subject to court approval.
